m: a heavy message the prophet lifts up and delivers
fiercely loyal, like a spouse who will not share
a roaring windstorm with its rain
angry because a wrong has been done
a hilltop fort you run to when an army comes
the dry stalks left standing in a cut field, burned at once
go on your holy-day trips to the Temple again, free to travel
get ready for the blow (the Hebrew says "strengthen the loins," the body's middle)
bright red cloth, a color of war and wealth
a roofed shield that protected soldiers who attacked a wall
the hips and lower back, where Hebrew felt terror and labor pains
the half-grown lions that hunt with the pride
whole extended families and peoples
the long hem of a woman's robe
the outer wall or mound that guarded a city
the first ripe figs of the year, so ripe they drop at a touch
a wooden frame used to shape wet clay into bricks
the king's secretaries and officials who ran the empire
your kings and rulers, called shepherds of the people
claps, as people do to cheer, or to mock
